content: This mechanism acts directly on the T cell and does not require restoring C9orf72 expression in CD14+ monocytes, so it is not undermined by the fact that the predicted reversal of that monocyte-expression route (restoring monocyte C9orf72 to restore tolerance) was already found not to hold in this knowledge base.

IL-17A signalling sustains CD80 surface trafficking on C9orf72-deficient myeloid cells/microglia; genetic Il17a deletion or systemic anti-IL-17A antibody treatment reverses CD80 accumulation, reduces neuroinflammation and improves motor performance in C9orf72-deficient mice (restates C-789/C-153/C-666; all rest on a source whose quotes mcp__literature__check_quote reports as unverifiable — text not available).
context: C9orf72 myeloid/microglial-conditional knockout mice, secondary synthesis of PMC11247723 (verification caveat: not independently quote-verified)
mechanism: IL-17A sustains surface trafficking of CD80 on C9orf72-deficient macrophages, monocytes and microglia; Il17a deletion prevents CD80 enrichment and antibody neutralization improves motor performance and suppresses neuroinflammation, indicating an interventionally tested causal driver, not merely a correlate.

content: The correlational IL-10-survival association reported in Michaelis et al. reflects a causal protective relationship rather than reverse causation (slower progressors simply having more time to mount the response) or confounding by disease stage; this is a necessary assumption for c2 to be a therapeutic rationale rather than a biomarker.

The anergy/Tr1-conversion mechanism shown for myelin peptides in a mouse EAE model and judged well tolerated in a 6-patient MS phase 1 trial generalizes across antigen (myelin to C9orf72), species (mouse to human) and disease (MS to ALS); none of this has been tested for C9orf72 peptides specifically.

Even if the innate IL-17A/CD80 axis (c1-c5) is fully suppressed, motor neurons may still be injured by the separate, immune-independent gain-of-function dipeptide-repeat (polyGR) proteotoxicity arm acting synergistically with the LOF proteostasis deficit, so the proposed intervention is not expected to be sufficient on its own to halt motor neuron loss (restates C-507).
mechanism: Combined failure of autophagic clearance and accumulation of toxic dipeptide-repeat species exceeds neuronal stress-response capacity, as already established in C-507; this pathway is immune-independent and not addressed by c5/c6.

content: A higher IL-10-mediated C9orf72-specific T-cell response is associated with slower ALS disease progression, so an intervention-driven rise in this response is predicted to slow progression.
mechanism: As already framed in this knowledge base, a response skewed toward IL-10 leaves the inflammatory component of the C9orf72-specific response relatively unopposed when IL-10 is low; raising the IL-10 arm is extrapolated, from the observed association between higher IL-10-mediated response and longer survival, to slow progression -- an association, not yet a demonstrated causal effect of any intervention.

content: CD80-driven neuroinflammation in the C9orf72-deficient myeloid/microglial compartment contributes to motor neuron damage, through a route independent of the adaptive CD4+ T-cell response.
context: C9orf72-ALS, innate-immune route, distinct from the adaptive CD4+ T-cell route in C-44/C-773
mechanism: Persistent myeloid/microglial CD80-costimulatory and pro-inflammatory activity damages motor neurons via standard neuroinflammatory mediators (ROS, TNF, excitotoxic glutamate release from activated microglia), adding to rather than explaining away the separate LOF+GOF proteostasis-driven injury already established in C-507.

content: Chronic, adjuvant-free subcutaneous dosing of a peptide panel built from the mapped immunodominant C9orf72 epitopes, matched to a patient's HLA-DRB1/DQB1 restriction, re-engages C9orf72-cognate TCRs repeatedly without costimulatory danger signal, converting already-polarized clones toward an IL-10-dominant, Foxp3-independent Tr1-like anergic state, producing a peripheral tolerogenic immune state.
context: C9orf72-ALS patients carrying one of the mapped HLA-DRB1*14:01/03:01/01:02 or DQB1*05:01 restrictions
mechanism: Extrapolated from the ATX-MS-1467 myelin-peptide platform, where chronic adjuvant-free dosing produced an enduring shift from a pro-inflammatory to a tolerogenic peripheral state in a mouse EAE model and was well tolerated in a 6-patient MS phase 1 trial; untested here for the C9orf72 antigen, human ALS T cells, or already-primed (not only naive) clones.

content: The induced peripheral tolerogenic state raises the share of the C9orf72-specific T-cell response running through the IL-10 arm.
context: C9orf72-ALS patients under chronic peptide dosing
mechanism: Antigen-specific conversion of engaged clones to an IL-10-dominant anergic/Tr1 phenotype increases the fraction of the C9orf72-specific response carried by the IL-10 arm relative to the inflammatory arm.

content: The STING/IL-17A/CD80 mechanism (c1-c4) is established in C9orf72 complete or myeloid-lineage conditional knockout mice, not in human C9orf72 repeat-expansion carriers, who retain partial (haploinsufficient) rather than null C9orf72 expression; whether partial loss suffices to trigger the same cascade in human myeloid cells/microglia is unknown.

A multi-epitope C9orf72 peptide pool can achieve adequate HLA-restricted coverage for priming, despite the absence of a single validated immunodominant epitope and despite apparent epitope clustering being attributable to overlapping-peptide artifact rather than independently confirmed immunodominant cores.
A higher IL-10-mediated C9orf72-specific T cell response is associated with slower ALS disease progression; raising this response is therefore treated as the therapeutic lever.
context: individuals with ALS, autoreactive CD4+ T cell response to C9orf72 (Michaelis et al. 2025)
mechanism: A response skewed away from the IL-10 arm is proposed to leave the inflammatory component of the C9orf72-specific response relatively unopposed; this restates C-832's framing as the basis for treating IL-10 magnitude as a therapeutic target.

content: Because the targeted axis (myeloid-intrinsic IL-17A/CD80 signalling) is a broad, antigen-non-specific innate program rather than part of antigen-specific adaptive tolerance, restricting the blockade to the myeloid/microglial compartment is assumed to preserve systemic immune competence against unrelated antigens better than systemic Treg-IL-2 infusion (C-754/C-755) or systemic GM-CSF (C-756).
context: C9orf72-ALS, proposed intervention, contrasted with systemic Treg/IL-2 and GM-CSF strategies already in the knowledge base
mechanism: Restricting delivery/action to the chronically-activated myeloid/microglial compartment is a narrower perturbation than systemically modulating Treg number/function or T-cell costimulation genome-wide; this is an assumption about delivery selectivity, not a demonstrated result.

content: In the absence of exogenous tolerogenic signal, loss of peripheral tolerance to C9orf72 lets escaped autoreactive CD4+ clones default toward a Th2/Th17-skewed rather than regulatory/Tr1 fate.
context: C9orf72-ALS, peripheral and CNS-draining lymphoid compartments, absent tolerogenic co-signalling
mechanism: Escape from peripheral deletion/anergy lets engaged clones differentiate along inflammatory rather than regulatory lines when TGF-beta/retinoic-acid-type tolerogenic co-signals are missing, as framed by the Th2-default mechanism and the myeloid CD80-driven Th17 axis already in this knowledge base.

content: Antigen-restricted priming confines the IL-2 boost mainly to C9orf72-reactive, antigen-experienced clones (via their transient CD25 upregulation), limiting expansion of the broader polyclonal Treg/effector pool compared with IL-2 given without antigen pairing, and thereby better preserving systemic immune competence.

Sustained STING pathway activity in C9orf72-deficient myeloid cells is assumed to promote IL-17A signalling, bridging the STING defect (c1) to the CD80/IL-17A-dependent phenotype reported independently in the same genetic model; this specific link has not itself been measured.
context: inferred bridge between two separately reported phenotypes of C9orf72-deficient myeloid cells; not directly measured in either source
mechanism: Type-I interferon signalling downstream of chronic STING activation is known in other inflammatory contexts to prime or amplify IL-17A-producing lymphocyte/innate lymphoid populations; whether this operates in C9orf72-deficient myeloid cells specifically is untested.

content: A myeloid/microglia-restricted blockade of IL-17A or CD80 signalling, rather than systemic T-cell costimulation blockade or non-specific Treg/IL-2 expansion, is predicted to interrupt the c1-c4 innate autoinflammatory chain and reduce motor neuron damage.
context: proposed intervention in C9orf72-ALS; not tested in any cited source
mechanism: Blocking IL-17A or CD80 at the chronically-activated myeloid/microglial compartment is predicted to interrupt the innate chain c1-c4 at its effector step, without altering circulating Treg number/function or the antigen-specific CD4+ Th2/IL-10 response.

content: Already-primed, effector-differentiated Th2/Th17 C9orf72-reactive clones -- not only naive ones -- remain susceptible to antigen-specific anergy or Tr1 conversion under chronic low-dose exposure. ALS patients at diagnosis, where the C9orf72-reactive repertoire was already mapped, likely carry an expanded, differentiated rather than purely naive population, and most tolerogenic-peptide evidence concerns naive or early-stage clones.

Because only TCRs cognate for the mapped C9orf72 HLA-peptide combinations are chronically re-engaged, the therapy does not raise Treg number or suppressive function across the whole repertoire and so preserves immune responses to other antigens, unlike low-dose IL-2, GM-CSF or polyclonal Treg infusion.
context: contrasted with Treg infusion+IL-2, low-dose IL-2 alone, and GM-CSF, all of which raise Treg number or suppressive function across the whole repertoire
mechanism: Restricting antigen exposure to C9orf72 epitopes tolerizes/converts only C9orf72-cognate clones, leaving pathogen- or tumour-antigen-specific clones and overall Treg/effector balance for other antigens closer to baseline than repertoire-wide Treg-boosting regimens would.

content: Reduced neuroinflammation/microglial neurotoxicity translates into reduced motor neuron injury; this link is assumed, not evidenced by any record available in this task.
context: general ALS neuroinflammation pathophysiology; no CNS-compartment data appear among the records available to me
mechanism: Activated, neurotoxic microglia are assumed to injure motor neurons directly or via cytokine/oxidative-stress signaling, so that any upstream dampening of microglial neurotoxicity propagates into reduced motor neuron injury; this step is extrapolated, not sourced, in the material I have.

content: The pre-existing Th2/Treg-like phenotype of C9orf72-reactive CD4+ T cells makes this population a receptive substrate for IL-2-driven stabilization toward IL-10 production, rather than requiring de novo induction of a regulatory fate from naive cells.

C9orf72 loss of function in myeloid cells (CD14+ monocytes, microglia) causes impaired STING protein degradation and sustained STING pathway activity, driving a type-I-interferon-dominated innate autoinflammatory program (restates verified literature claim C-795).
context: mouse genetic models, complete and myeloid-lineage-conditional C9orf72 knockout (McCauley et al. 2020)
mechanism: Loss of C9orf72 impairs autolysosomal degradation of STING, causing hyperresponsiveness to STING activation and sustained type-I interferon signalling in myeloid cells, independent of any single antigen's presentation.

content: C9orf72-ALS pathogenesis passes through a peripheral-tolerance-failure stage in which C9orf72-reactive CD4+ T cells escape anergy/deletion and persist as a mixed population whose IL-10-dominant vs IL-5/IL-17-dominant balance determines downstream neuroinflammatory load, rather than the two cytokine programmes being fixed, non-interconvertible lineages.

Low-dose IL-2 dosing can be titrated, as piloted safely in ALS Treg+IL-2 trials and shown to sustain Treg suppressive function for 12 months in a GM-CSF trial in Parkinson's disease, without substantially expanding CD25-intermediate effector T cell populations.
Th2/Treg-associated cytokines, including IL-10, dampen neuroinflammation and microglial neurotoxicity, giving a candidate downstream route from the T-cell cytokine shift to neuroprotection.
context: candidate cellular mechanism linking IL-10-associated regulatory responses to neuroprotection in ALS
mechanism: IL-4 directly suppresses microglial neurotoxicity without cell contact, and more broadly Th2/Treg-associated cytokines dampen neuroinflammatory activity; this restates C-838.

content: Sequential C9orf72-epitope peptide priming followed by a low-dose IL-2 boost increases the durable frequency of IL-10-producing C9orf72-specific CD4+ T cells more than either modality alone; never tested in ALS or for this antigen.
context: ALS patients, C9orf72 repeat-expansion carriers; novel combination, extrapolated from antigen-specific peptide platforms (e.g. ATX-MS-1467) and from IL-2-based Treg modulation (ex vivo Treg+IL-2 infusion, GM-CSF), none tested together or in this antigen/disease pairing
mechanism: Low-dose IL-2 signals preferentially through the high-affinity IL-2 receptor (CD25) transiently upregulated on T cells recently engaged by cognate antigen; delivered after C9orf72-peptide priming it is hypothesized to selectively expand and stabilize the IL-10-producing fraction of the already antigen-engaged clone population, unlike IL-2 given without antigen pairing or generic Treg-function boosting that act on the repertoire irrespective of specificity.
